setup: Set both pulleys to the lowest position on a dual-cable column station and attach single D-handles.
Grasp a handle in each hand with palms facing forward and slightly upward.
Take a step forward into a staggered stance to create tension on the cables, keeping the chest tall and a slight bend in both elbows.
steps: Brace your core and maintain a fixed, slight bend in the elbows.
Sweep your hands upward and inward along an arc, bringing them together around upper-chest or neck height.
Squeeze your upper chest firmly at the top of the contraction for a brief pause.
Lower the handles slowly back along the same path under control until you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you bring your hands upward together; inhale as you lower them under control.
cues: Scoop your hands up and in
Keep the elbows locked in a soft bend

common_faults.fault: Turning the movement into a bicep curl by flexing and extending the elbows.
common_faults.correction: Lock a slight bend into your elbows at the start and keep that joint angle fixed throughout the entire rep.

common_faults.fault: Using excessive momentum and swinging the torso forward and backward.
common_faults.correction: Adopt a stable staggered stance, brace your midsection, and keep your torso stationary.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders upward toward the ears during the fly.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulder blades depressed and engage the chest rather than the upper trapezius to drive the motion.

precautions: Avoid over-extending behind the shoulder joint in the bottom position if you experience anterior shoulder discomfort.

name: Cable Low-to-High Fly
summary: A standing cable isolation exercise that targets the upper chest and anterior deltoids by sweeping the handles upward and together.
